title: Cannot map to Win + Ctrl + L

judgment.rationale: The issue is already being handled by an upstream PR that blocks any chord containing Win+L, which matches the discussion in the issue thread.
evidence: A maintainer clarified in the issue that plain Win+L is reserved by Windows, while Win+Ctrl+L is a different shortcut whose current remap UX still breaks silently.
The reporter explicitly reframed the request as preventing or warning on chords involving Win+L rather than insisting on unsupported remapping.
Open PR #49759 says it fixes #49725 by updating shortcut validation so any shortcut containing both Win and L is flagged as illegal.
That PR matches the issue discussion's likely resolution: block the unsupported mapping in the UI instead of letting it fail silently at runtime.
judgment.recommended_action: Track PR #49759 and verify the editor now surfaces the illegal-shortcut warning for Win+L supersets.

fix_assessment.rationale: A focused upstream fix attempt already exists and aligns with the issue's accepted direction.

issue_context.summary: Mapping to Win+Ctrl+L currently breaks because Windows captures the Win+L subset first. The issue discussion already converged on blocking such mappings in the UI, and PR #49759 implements that approach.
known_information: The issue originates from Keyboard Manager on PowerToys 0.100.1 and uses Win+Ctrl+L / Live Captions as the motivating example.
A maintainer first noted that Win+L is hard-wired, then clarified that Win+Ctrl+L is distinct but currently affected by simultaneous key ordering and validation limitations.
The reporter agreed that surfacing this limitation in-product would be a better experience than silent failure.
PR #49759 now proposes to reject any chord containing both Win and L in the validation helper.
inferences: The accepted product direction is now clear: warn/block the mapping rather than attempt an unreliable runtime workaround.
Because a contributor already implemented that exact behavior in an open PR, additional design work in this batch would be duplicative.
issue_context.analysis: This is a straightforward handled issue. The issue discussion already did the product design work publicly, and the linked PR implements it. The dashboard should keep the issue attached to that PR instead of reopening its validity.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the full issue body and all public comments in the live issue state.
Reviewed PR #49759 to confirm it explicitly closes #49725 and blocks any shortcut containing Win+L.
Compared the PR approach with the maintainer/reporter discussion and confirmed they align.

author: zhizhongpu

confidence.rationale: The issue discussion and linked PR agree on the resolution: block unsupported Win+L supersets in the UI.
